answers_to_your_questions.answer: Answering all three desk questions directly. (a) Origination direction does NOT change the MU evidence_for rewrite from round 2. That rewrite led with the $12.40/GB native contract_quote (2026-09-20, tier1) on its own merits -- freshest datapoint, unambiguously HBM3E-labeled by its own generation key with no duplication question attached to it -- not because the $9.00 figure was 'really HBM3's'. Whether $9.00 originated on hbm3e and was duplicated onto hbm3, or the reverse, the $12.40 print was still the better lead. So the rewrite stands, but for the reason I gave at the time (freshness/unambiguity), not for the reason M2.6's framing implied (that $9.00 belonged to the other generation) -- that framing was wrong and I should not have passed it forward uncritically. (b) No, $9.00 is not safe to cite for EITHER generation right now. Cycle's finding is correct: C1 is filed on hbm3e.usd_per_gb and describes those exact points as HBM3E's own ($300/36GB), which means hbm3's identical series is the unexplained one -- but 'C1 says it's HBM3E's' is still the tracker's self-description, not an independent resolution of why hbm3 carries the same numbers. I am not resolving this by inference either. Until the tracker owner (hbm-tracker skill) files a real fix, I am treating the $9.00 stack_derived figure as UNCITABLE for direction on either generation, full stop -- which is already reflected in MU's current evidence (it no longer appears there since round 2). (c) I checked every thesis entry and thesis_tensions line I have written this run: none of them assert an HBM3 (plain, non-E) direction read. My hbm3-generation citations were limited to the now-removed MU line and a context-only mention in my original task output that HBM3 stack_derived was 'flat' -- that line was descriptive scene-setting, not load-bearing for any verdict, and I am retracting it as unsafe rather than defending it. On the second matter (the -18.92% TrendForce segment): I did not author M2.8/M3.22's framing and have not treated that segment as contradicting C1 anywhere in MU's or SKHY's evidence -- my citations of C1 have consistently used the corrected_view (rising/flat, not the pre-flip decline), so no correction needed on my side there, but I've noted cycle's point for the record: the -18.92% segment ends 2026-01-15, exactly where C1 says the repricing begins, so it is pre-flip and must not be read as current.
